evals.prompt: sys.dm_exec_requests shows session 84 blocked by 71 with wait_type LCK_M_U and wait_time 42117, and session 92 blocked by 84 with LCK_M_S wait_time 38004. Session 71 has status sleeping, wait_type NULL, open_transaction_count 1, last_request_end_time 6 minutes ago, program_name OrderEntry.exe, input buffer 'UPDATE dbo.Orders SET Status = 0x48 WHERE OrderId = 4711'. blocked process threshold (s) is 0.
evals.expected_output: BL1 head blocker is session 71. BL9 Critical (sleeping session with open transaction — will not self-resolve). BL10 Critical (6 minutes idle — orphaned transaction after a client timeout or cancel). BL2 Critical (42 s lock wait). BL3 Warning (2-level chain). BL31 Warning (blocked process threshold off, so the next occurrence is not captured). Immediate relief: KILL 71, stating the rollback cost. Durable fix: roll back in the client error handler (IF @@TRANCOUNT > 0 ROLLBACK TRAN) or SET XACT_ABORT ON; set blocked process threshold and create a blocked_process_report XE session. Do not kill sessions 84 or 92 — they are victims.

evals.prompt: Fourteen sessions are waiting on LCK_M_IS against dbo.Orders. sys.dm_tran_locks shows session 71 holding a single OBJECT lock with request_mode X and request_status GRANT on that table, and no KEY or PAGE locks for that session. The blocker is running 'DELETE FROM dbo.LogMessages WHERE LogDate < 20250102' under a single transaction. Trace flag 1211 is not enabled and the database has is_read_committed_snapshot_on = 0.
evals.expected_output: BL16 Critical (lock escalation — OBJECT lock in X mode with row and page locks gone; an intent-mode OBJECT lock would not be escalation). BL4 Critical (fan-out of 14). BL23 Critical (footprint crossed the 5,000-lock escalation threshold). BL29 Warning (read-only victims would not block under RCSI). Fixes ranked: batch the DELETE with DELETE TOP (1000) in a loop, tune indexes to reduce the lock footprint, consider per-table LOCK_ESCALATION = DISABLE only as a temporary measure, and note that trace flags 1211/1224 risk error 1204 by removing the lock-memory cap.

evals.prompt: Blocked process report XML shows a blocking-process with status sleeping, trancount 1, and inputbuf 'SELECT TOP 100 * FROM dbo.Inventory', client interface 'Microsoft JDBC Driver'. The blocked-process shows waittime 61000 and lockMode U on a KEY resource. Same pattern appears in three reports over two days.
evals.expected_output: BL27 Critical (implicit transactions — an open transaction with no BEGIN TRAN in the input buffer, from a driver that sets IMPLICIT_TRANSACTIONS ON). BL9 Critical (sleeping session holding locks). BL2 Critical (61 s wait). BL7 Critical (same head blocker across three captures — a design defect, not an incident). Fix: turn off implicit transactions at the driver/connection or commit explicitly after each unit of work; kill the session for immediate relief. Note that the last statement shown is not necessarily the one holding the locks — capture sql_batch_completed to see the earlier statements in the transaction.

evals.prompt: sp_WhoIsActive @find_block_leaders = 1 shows session 54 at the top with blocked_session_count 11, running 'SELECT ... FROM dbo.Orders WHERE OrderDate >= @p1' for 14 minutes, status suspended, wait_info NULL. Directly under it session 61 is blocked by 54 waiting LCK_M_SCH_M running 'ALTER INDEX IX_Orders_CustomerId ON dbo.Orders REBUILD'. Sessions 72, 78, 83 and seven others are blocked by 61 waiting LCK_M_SCH_S on simple single-row SELECTs and INSERTs.
evals.expected_output: BL43 Critical — the apparent head blocker (54) is a benign reader; the real cost is the Sch-M index rebuild (61) queued behind it, and lock requests queue in order so the ten sessions behind 61 are blocked by the rebuild, not by the SELECT. BL18 Critical (Sch-M blocking Sch-S), BL4 Critical (fan-out), BL15 Warning (index maintenance during production). Killing 54 releases the rebuild, which is the more disruptive operation — say so. Fix: ALTER INDEX ... REBUILD WITH (ONLINE = ON (WAIT_AT_LOW_PRIORITY (MAX_DURATION = n MINUTES, ABORT_AFTER_WAIT = SELF))), set the equivalent parameters in the maintenance job, and move it to a quiet window; separately shorten or offload the 14-minute report (BL8).

evals.prompt: The blocking happened yesterday and nobody captured it. sp_BlitzFirst @SinceStartup = 1 shows LCK_M_S at 28% of wait time. sys.dm_db_index_operational_stats for the database shows PK_Orders with row_lock_wait_in_ms 412004 over 1204 waits and index_lock_promotion_attempt_count 38 with index_lock_promotion_count 2; every other index is under 20000 ms. blocked process threshold (s) is 0 and there is no Extended Events session for blocked_process_report. The database has is_read_committed_snapshot_on = 0.
evals.expected_output: BL37 Critical (LCK_M_S at 28% of wait time with no chain captured — wait stats are recorded by victims, so they size the problem and can never name the blocker). BL38 Critical (PK_Orders carries the overwhelming majority of lock wait time, 342 ms average — that is where to look). BL39 Critical (38 escalation attempts against 2 completions: a large lock footprint repeatedly refused escalation because another session held an incompatible table lock). BL29 Warning (LCK_M_S victims with RCSI off — readers would not wait at all under RCSI). BL31 Warning and BL33 Warning (nothing configured to capture the next occurrence). Next steps in order: set blocked process threshold to about 15-20 s and create a blocked_process_report XE session, batch or index the statement writing dbo.Orders, evaluate RCSI, and note the index counters reset with the metadata cache so they are 'roughly since restart', and exclude object/metadata/application lock waits.
